final_answer: Relocate ONLY the DONE-admission action-evidence guard — not the PARALLEL handler or the stagnation/no-progress logic — out of driver/85-loop-mode-transitions.ps1 into driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1. Insert it on semantic anchors (immediately after plannerStatus status-parse, inside the DONE∧normal-guard cluster, before the done-gate) rather than literal line offsets, because the line numbers (:1027 / :1433) are brittle and will drift. Before extraction, run a dependency analysis to lock the exact slice: the micro-debate left unresolved whether the surgical ~85:67-84 region captures all setup the guard depends on, so the boundary must be confirmed (slightly expanded if a dependency forces it) but kept far narrower than the literal 12-95 range. Harden the relocated block for StrictMode: defensively initialize every guard-local, treat helper failures as fail-closed CONTINUE with an explicit failure record, and keep $s.task_did_actions as the durable state carrier so the existing done-gate and downstream consumers are untouched. Fix the spurious-rejection metric by setting force_coder ONLY when the current active normal backlog task is genuinely rejected for missing_action_evidence (with task/backlog identity matching) and by clearing any stale force_coder on accepted-DONE/closure paths. Recompute evidence at done-gate time primarily from durable, speaker-agnostic signals (git diff / state) while preserving explicitly-supported reply-based exceptions, so codex and claude turns evaluate identically. Validate with a deterministic regression test and a bounded pure-decision shadow stage (decision logged, no side effects) before live cutover, then gate the cutover through bridge_self_canary in an isolated worktree, requiring driver.ps1 -SelfTest and smoke.ps1 to pass, explicit operator authorization, and single-commit rollback notes. Reject the literal lines-12-95 extraction: it is the wrong scope, conflicts with the surgical consensus, and would drag unrelated PARALLEL/stagnation logic out of 85.

decisions.decision: Relocate only the DONE-admission action-evidence guard from driver/85-loop-mode-transitions.ps1, leaving the PARALLEL handler and stagnation/no-progress logic in place (atom_001).
decisions.rationale: Judge accept 0.898. The semantic scope is the correct unit of change: only the DONE-admission evidence check belongs in the completion-checks file. PARALLEL handling and stagnation detection are owned by 85 and are unrelated to the done path; moving them would expand the blast radius of a high-risk control-plane edit for no benefit.
alternatives_considered: Extract the literal block lines 12-95 as-is (atom_010, rejected)
Move the entire loop-mode-transitions DONE/PARALLEL cluster wholesale
decisions.risk: Mis-drawing the boundary could leave behind setup the guard depends on (incomplete relocation) or split interdependent logic — the unresolved micro-debate round-2 concern.
decisions.test: Diff confirms only the action-evidence/DONE portion moved; PARALLEL handler and stagnation detector still resolve and fire from 85 under driver.ps1 -SelfTest; no dangling references to moved symbols remain in 85.

decisions.decision: Insert the relocated guard in driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1 after plannerStatus status-parse and before the full DONE-gate, anchored on semantic markers (status-parse regex; DONE∧normal gate condition) rather than literal line numbers (atom_002).
decisions.rationale: Judge accept 0.8985. The guard must run after planner status is known but before DONE verification/closure. Semantic anchoring survives edits that shift :1027/:1433; literal-offset insertion is brittle and would silently land in the wrong place after any prior change.
alternatives_considered: Place before status-parse (would evaluate evidence without a known planner status)
decisions.risk: Wrong ordering relative to status-parse or done-gate reintroduces 'property/variable not found' or evaluates on stale status.
decisions.test: Execution-order assertion: guard runs after status parse and before the DONE gate in 86; insertion point sits inside the DONE∧normal-guard cluster; regression test confirms ordering on a real driver turn.

decisions.decision: Defensively initialize every guard-local value and treat helper failures as fail-closed CONTINUE with an explicit failure record (atom_003).
decisions.rationale: Judge accept 0.856. The ×6/session 'property/variable not found' metric is a StrictMode symptom of uninitialized locals on the done path. Defaulting all locals and recording (not swallowing) helper failures makes the guard StrictMode-safe and keeps failures diagnosable instead of producing silent CONTINUE loops.
alternatives_considered: Relax Set-StrictMode on the done path (hides the real defect)
Wrap in a broad try/catch that swallows errors silently
decisions.risk: Fail-closed CONTINUE could mask a genuine DONE if helpers fail systematically; the explicit failure record mitigates by surfacing the cause.
decisions.test: Canary scenarios with missing/uninitialized state assert zero StrictMode throws on the 86 done path and that a failure record is emitted on induced helper failure while behavior stays fail-closed.

decisions.decision: Set force_coder only when the current ACTIVE normal backlog task is rejected for missing_action_evidence, with explicit task/backlog identity matching, and clear any stale force_coder on accepted-DONE/closure paths (atom_004, modified per judge).
decisions.rationale: Judge modify 0.823 (penalty 0.04). Direction is correct but under-specified: scoping force_coder to a real missing_action_evidence rejection eliminates spurious rejections, and the modification adds task-identity matching plus stale-flag clearing so a force_coder set on a prior task cannot survive into the turn after an accepted DONE — the exact spurious-flip metric.
alternatives_considered: Set force_coder on any DONE rejection regardless of task identity (original atom_004)
decisions.risk: Identity check must use the durable task id; a mismatch in how active-task identity is derived could either fail to clear a stale flag or clear a legitimately-needed one.
decisions.test: Canary: accepted DONE then next turn asserts no force_coder/CONTINUE flip; rejection on a non-active or mismatched-identity task does not raise force_coder; stale force_coder is cleared on the accepted-DONE/closure path.

decisions.decision: Make durable, speaker-agnostic signals (git diff / state) the primary evidence source at done-gate time, while preserving explicitly-supported reply-based exceptions and the existing state contract (atom_006, modified per judge).
decisions.rationale: Judge modify 0.668 (penalty 0.05). Recomputing evidence from durable signals removes the speaker-context mismatch (codex vs claude turn) that drives wrong evidence. As written the atom was too broad and risked discarding intentional verified/covered reply paths and implying a costly redesign; the modification keeps it scoped to refreshing the evidence value, not re-architecting the evidence model.
alternatives_considered: Full redesign replacing all reply-based evidence (original atom_006)
Keep turn-specific reply evidence as primary (status quo, causes mismatch)
decisions.risk: Higher implementation cost and feasibility risk (judge feasibility 0.58); over-reach could drop legitimate reply-verified evidence paths.
decisions.test: Evidence computed for both codex and claude turns is identical for the same durable state; explicitly-supported reply exceptions still pass; no change to the $s.task_did_actions read/write contract.

decisions.decision: Preserve $s.task_did_actions as the durable carrier read/written by the done-gate and other consumers; evidence recomputation refreshes this value rather than replacing the contract (atom_007).
decisions.rationale: Judge accept 0.87. Keeping the established state contract avoids breaking the done-gate and downstream consumers, and lets atom_006's recomputation slot in by updating the existing field instead of introducing a parallel state channel.
alternatives_considered: Introduce a new evidence state field and migrate consumers
Compute evidence inline at each consumer
decisions.risk: Low; if recomputation writes the field at the wrong phase, a consumer could read a stale value.
decisions.test: Assert $s.task_did_actions is written before and read correctly by the done-gate and every other consumer; value reflects the recomputed durable evidence.

decisions.decision: Add a deterministic regression test (e.g. test-driver-done-guard-relocation.ps1) asserting no StrictMode throws and no spurious force_coder flips after an accepted DONE, and integrate it into the control-plane gate (atom_009).
decisions.rationale: Judge accept 0.799 (penalty 0.02). This test directly covers the two target metrics (property/variable-not-found → 0; spurious force_coder → 0) and the relocation's specific failure mode, turning the success criteria into an automated guard against regression.
alternatives_considered: Manual canary observation without a committed regression test
decisions.risk: Control-plane gate integration adds maintenance cost; a flaky or under-specified test could block legitimate changes.
decisions.test: Run test-driver-done-guard-relocation.ps1; assert pass for both the StrictMode-safety and post-accepted-DONE force_coder conditions; confirm it is wired into the control-plane gate.

decisions.decision: Run a bounded pure-decision observe-only/shadow stage before live cutover: refactor the guard into a side-effect-free decision function, log the new-location decision alongside the old for K sessions, and compare (atom_008, modified per judge).
decisions.rationale: Judge modify 0.614 (penalty 0.06). Shadow validation is valuable but unsafe if it runs two live guards with side effects (duplicate mutations / double CONTINUE). The modification requires first extracting a pure decision path so only logging differs, making old≡new comparison safe and meaningful.
alternatives_considered: Run old and new live guards side-by-side without isolation (rejected as risky)
Skip shadowing and cut over directly behind the canary gate
decisions.risk: Refactor-to-pure adds work; if side effects aren't fully isolated, shadowing duplicates mutations. K must be chosen large enough to be representative.
decisions.test: For K sessions, shadow log shows new-location decision == old-location decision with zero target-metric occurrences and zero duplicated side effects.

decisions.decision: Gate the cutover through bridge_self_canary in an isolated worktree, requiring driver.ps1 -SelfTest and smoke.ps1 to pass, explicit operator authorization, and comprehensive single-commit rollback notes (atom_005).
decisions.rationale: Judge accept 0.84 (penalty 0.02). This is a high-risk control-plane edit to 85/86; canary + SelfTest + smoke + explicit operator sign-off + a one-commit revert path materially reduce cutover risk and satisfy the task's hard safety constraints.
alternatives_considered: Direct commit to master without canary
decisions.risk: Operator authorization is external to automated gating and cannot be self-granted; isolated-worktree setup is not zero-cost in every environment.
decisions.test: Execute bridge_self_canary; SelfTest and smoke both pass; operator authorization is recorded; a single-commit revert is prepared and dry-run verified.

rejected.decision: Extract literal lines 12-95 from driver/85-loop-mode-transitions.ps1 as the action-evidence DONE-guard block (atom_010).
rejected.why: Judge reject 0.35 (correctness 0.05, penalties 0.15 + 0.08). The 12-95 range is overbroad and includes unrelated PARALLEL and stagnation/no-progress logic, directly conflicting with the surgical-relocation consensus (atom_001). The micro-debate resolved in favor of minimal, targeted change; moving the whole literal block would relocate unrelated behavior out of 85 and sharply increase regression risk on a control-plane edit.

open_questions: What is the exact semantic boundary of the DONE-admission action-evidence guard within 85:12-95? Micro-debate round 2 left unresolved whether the ~85:67-84 slice captures all setup/related checks or must be slightly (but still narrowly) expanded — a dependency analysis must confirm before extraction.
Which specific reply-based evidence exceptions are 'explicitly supported' and must be preserved when durable speaker-agnostic evidence becomes primary (atom_006 modify)?
How many shadow sessions K are required for the observe-only stage to be representative before live cutover (atom_008)?
Is operator authorization scoped to this single cutover, or standing for the parent control-plane change family — and who is the authorizing operator of record?
Exactly how is 'active normal backlog task identity' derived for the force_coder identity match (which durable task id field), to ensure stale-flag clearing is reliable (atom_004 modify)?
implementation_plan: 1. In an isolated worktree (bridge_self_canary), run a dependency analysis over 85:12-95 to lock the exact surgical slice of the DONE-admission action-evidence guard, confirming the PARALLEL handler and stagnation/no-progress logic are excluded and any required setup is included (resolves atom_001 vs atom_010 conflict and the micro-debate round-2 question).

2. Refactor the guard into a side-effect-free pure decision function so its CONTINUE/force_coder/evidence decision can be evaluated without mutating state (prerequisite for safe shadowing — atom_008).
3. Harden the function for StrictMode: defensively initialize all guard-locals; treat helper failures as fail-closed CONTINUE with an explicit failure record (atom_003).

4. Constrain force_coder: set it only on a real missing_action_evidence rejection of the active normal backlog task with explicit task/backlog identity matching, and clear stale force_coder on accepted-DONE/closure paths (atom_004 modified).

5. Recompute action evidence from durable speaker-agnostic signals (git diff/state) as primary, preserving explicitly-supported reply-based exceptions; continue writing/reading $s.task_did_actions as the durable carrier (atom_006 modified + atom_007).

6. Insert the hardened guard into driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1 anchored on semantic markers — after plannerStatus status-parse, inside the DONE∧normal-guard cluster, before the done-gate — not on literal line offsets (atom_002).

7. Add deterministic regression test test-driver-done-guard-relocation.ps1 (zero StrictMode throws; no spurious force_coder flip after accepted DONE) and wire it into the control-plane gate (atom_009).
8. Run the bounded pure-decision shadow stage for K sessions, logging new-location decision alongside old; require old≡new and zero target-metric occurrences before proceeding (atom_008 modified).

9. Execute the bridge_self_canary gate: driver.ps1 -SelfTest and smoke.ps1 must pass; collect canary evidence; verify the two target metrics (property/variable-not-found and spurious force_coder) are both 0 (atom_005).
10. Prepare single-commit rollback notes and dry-run the revert; obtain explicit operator authorization; only then cut over to live (atom_005).
next_step: In an isolated bridge_self_canary worktree, run the dependency analysis over driver/85-loop-mode-transitions.ps1:12-95 to lock the exact surgical boundary of the DONE-admission action-evidence guard (confirming PARALLEL and stagnation logic are excluded) — this unblocks the extraction and resolves the atom_001 vs atom_010 scope conflict.

red_team_findings.what: The action-evidence block (85:67-84) is NOT separable from the stagnation/no-progress detector; the decision's core claim that it can be surgically moved while 'leaving stagnation in place' is contradicted by the code.
red_team_findings.why: In driver/85-loop-mode-transitions.ps1 the evidence computation lives inside the `if ($speaker -eq 'codex' -and $mode -ne 'discuss')` stagnation block (line 52). It reads `$hasChanges` (set at 66) and sets `$hasChanges=$true` at lines 76 and 81 from Get-TaskActionEvidence and Test-TaskCoveredVerifiedDoneEvidence. The no-progress branch at 86-100 (`if ($hasChanges) {reset} else {increment + Activate-Doctor}`) DEPENDS on those augmentations. Extracting ~67-84 strips the action-evidence and covered-verified contributions from `$hasChanges`, so stagnation falls back to only the cruder `git -C $bridgeRoot diff --stat HEAD` (line 53) and will false-positive 'no progress' on turns where real work exists in the effective project repo — spuriously firing Activate-Doctor/Doctor. Both the rejected 12-95 boundary AND the accepted ~67-84 boundary are wrong; a correct fix must duplicate or restructure the shared signal, which the plan does not budget for and the 'dependency analysis' open question has not resolved.

red_team_findings.what: atom_003's 'fail-closed CONTINUE' inverts the current fail-OPEN behavior and creates a livelock risk that can brick the autonomous loop, with hard recovery.
red_team_findings.why: Today, evidence computation is wrapped in `try {...} catch {}` with a SILENT empty catch (85:69-83): a helper failure leaves task_did_actions unset, so the done-gate (86:1439) sees didActions=false and the task CLOSES (fail-open). The decision flips this to 'fail-closed CONTINUE with a failure record' — meaning a persistent helper fault now REJECTS every DONE and forces CONTINUE forever, never closing a genuinely-finished task. Because the driver loop runs the agent, this is a self-inflicted livelock. proposal_B explicitly warned a control-plane edit can 'deadlock or infinite force_coder' the autopilot. The shadow stage runs ON the driver being modified, and per repo memory the coder sandbox cannot reach .git, so automated rollback of a livelocked driver is non-trivial. The decision presents fail-closed as unambiguously 'safe' without acknowledging it changes the failure semantics from close-anyway to never-close.

red_team_findings.what: The contract's literal anchors are wrong AND there is no insertion point that satisfies both 'after planner status-parse' and 'triggered on every driver turn'.
red_team_findings.why: In 86: `:1027` is inside the fast-lane `if ($coderStatus -eq 'DONE')` block (1024-1032), not 'immediately after status-parse'; the planner status is parsed at 1036 inside `if ($speaker -eq 'claude')`; `:1433` is the STUDY gate, while the real normal action-evidence done-gate is 1438-1463. More importantly: the original write fires on CODEX turns (85:52), but the only place 'after status-parse' that has `$plannerStatus` for the planner decision is inside the claude-only block (1034+), which never runs on codex turns. Placing the guard before 1034 means plannerStatus isn't parsed yet; placing it after means it won't run on codex turns — violating the 'every driver turn' constraint and success_test #10. The decision's 'semantic anchoring' hand-waves this speaker/every-turn contradiction rather than resolving it, and also short-circuits exist between the proposed point and the gate (decomposition `continue` at 1043, parallel dispatch at 1050+).

red_team_findings.what: The 'spurious force_coder' success metric is likely unfixable within the stated 85→86 relocation scope; its source is never identified.
red_team_findings.why: force_coder is written in 7 sites in driver/83-loop-agent-turn.ps1 (287,308,390,405,422,528,538) and 4 in 86 (955,976,1216,1354). The task contract scopes the authorized control-plane change to relocating the guard from 85 to 86. atom_004 narrows force_coder to 'active normal task rejected for missing_action_evidence' but never pins WHICH write produces the post-accepted-DONE flip. If the spurious flip originates in 83 (the most active force_coder writer, out of the relocation scope), then (a) the relocation cannot move the metric to 0, and (b) fixing it expands the blast radius to a third control-plane file that the canary/operator-authorization/regression plan was scoped around 85/86 only. proposal_A even flags 'force_coder may still be set from stale state after task closure' — left unmitigated here.

red_team_findings.what: Moving the task_did_actions producer from very-early 85 to mid-86 (after ~1027) reorders it relative to ~18 consumers/writers, with the affected set explicitly unanalyzed.
red_team_findings.why: task_did_actions is read/written at 86:967,977,990,1193,1314,1350,1370,1439,1455,1503,1529,1551,1573,1759,1841, plus 86-loop-completion-cleanup (768,792,808), 86-loop-completion-actions (75), and 87. The current write at 85:84 happens before the turn increment, so all of 86 sees it. After relocation to >1027, consumers/writers at 86:967-990 run BEFORE the new write, and the covered-after-restart reset (1455) sets it false within the same gate. The decision (atom_007) and open_question #5 admit a stale-read/write-ordering hazard 'whose read-ordering could be affected' but defer it — shipping a high-risk reordering across a self-modifying control plane on a 'verify later' basis.

red_team_findings.what: SelfTest/smoke are relied on as the safety evidence but are not shown to exercise the relocated guard's runtime paths (StrictMode, missing-state, post-DONE force_coder).
red_team_findings.why: smoke.ps1 step 9 (line 164) runs `driver.ps1 -SelfTest` as a ParseFile + child-process load check and references canary checks; there is no evidence either drives a real normal-DONE turn through the moved guard. atom_005's own risk note concedes a canary 'that does not exercise the StrictMode/force_coder paths could pass while latent defects ship.' The plan's primary gates (SelfTest+smoke pass) are therefore weak/possibly-vacuous evidence for THIS change. The compensating regression test (atom_009) is authored by the same change and wired into the very gate it must itself pass — a bootstrap with no independent validation that it actually triggers the StrictMode throw / force_coder flip it claims to assert against.

red_team_findings.what: The decision is a plan, so the output_format and the execution-dependent success_tests are unmet as delivered.
red_team_findings.why: output_format requires 'implemented code changes ... evidence of successful canary execution, results from driver.ps1 -SelfTest and smoke.ps1, and prepared rollback notes,' and next_step is still 'run the dependency analysis ... before any code is moved.' No code is moved, no canary evidence, no SelfTest/smoke results, no operator authorization, no rollback notes exist yet. Success_tests requiring executed proof (SelfTest passes, smoke passes, canary completes with positive evidence, operator authorization obtained, rollback notes documented, both metrics→0) are all forward-looking promises, none satisfiable by the record itself. Additionally, two metric-critical implementation parameters remain open questions — the exact guard boundary and the shadow session count K / equivalence threshold — meaning the 'final' decision cannot yet be executed deterministically.
